findings.title: Reminder-cancellation calls are fire-and-forget; the cancelled flag may never be persisted
findings.body: In the cancellation flow, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` are invoked inside `Array.forEach` without being awaited. The whole fix depends on the `workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })` (or row delete) inside those async functions actually completing. The previous implementation collected the Prisma `deleteMany` promises and awaited them in `Promise.all`; now nothing is awaited, so the handler can return (and on serverless platforms like Vercel the function can be frozen) before the DB writes run, silently leaving reminders un-cancelled — the exact bug this PR fixes. The same un-awaited pattern was introduced at the other call sites: `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (requestReschedule, ~line 490), `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` (~line 966) and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` (lines 212-218, 376-382, 519-525, 574-580). These should be collected into an array of promises and awaited.

findings.title: immediateDelete path cancels in SendGrid but leaves stale DB rows and long-lived pending cancellations
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` only POSTs the cancel to SendGrid and returns — it neither deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row nor sets `cancelled: true`. For the workflow-delete and step-delete callers this is masked by the DB cascade, but in the reschedule path (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` line 968) the old booking's reminder rows stay in the database with `scheduled=true`, `cancelled=null` until their `scheduledDate` passes and the cron's past-date `deleteMany` happens to remove them. Worse, the reschedule path still cancels immediately in SendGrid for sends up to 72h out, and per the PR description such pending cancellations sit in SendGrid's `scheduled_sends` until the scheduled date and count toward the 100-pending-cancellations limit — the exact limit whose exhaustion caused this bug. Reschedules should use the same deferred mechanism (set `cancelled=true`, let the cron cancel within the final hour, and delete/flag the row) instead of `immediateDelete`.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid request aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders in that cron run
findings.body: In the new cancellation block, the `for` loop awaits `client.request(...)` sequentially, and any thrown error breaks out of the loop into the outer `catch`, skipping all not-yet-processed reminders in `remindersToCancel`. Additionally, the Prisma delete promises already accumulated for successfully cancelled reminders are never awaited in that case, so those rows are not deleted either (Prisma promises are lazy and only execute when awaited). This self-heals on the next cron run only as long as the reminders' `scheduledDate` has not passed; a reminder near the end of its 1-hour window whose cancellation request repeatedly fails (or is unlucky behind a failing one) will be sent by SendGrid. Consider wrapping each reminder's cancel+delete in its own try/catch so one failure doesn't affect the rest.
